description: Observations indicate pollination occurs through wind, water, or collision of free-floating particles.

label: biotic_unspecialised
description: Taxa are pollinated by a biotic agent, but do not have a specialist pollinator.

label: biotic_specialised
description: Taxa depend upon a specialist pollinator for pollen transfer.

label: animal
description: Flowers are observed to be animal-pollinated.

label: ballistic
description: Pollen is observed to be launched away from the plant by explosion.

label: bat
description: Flowers are observed to be bat-pollinated.

label: bee
description: Flowers are observed to be bee-pollinated.

label: beetle
description: Flowers are observed to be beetle-pollinated.

label: bird
description: Flowers are observed to be bird-pollinated.

label: butterfly
description: Flowers are observed to be butterfly-pollinated.

label: fly
description: Flowers are observed to be fly-pollinated.

label: insect
description: Flowers are observed to be insect-pollinated, type of insect not specified.

label: mammal
description: Flowers are observed to be mammal-pollinated.

label: moth
description: Flowers are observed to be moth-pollinated.

label: thrip
description: Flowers are observed to be thrip-pollinated.

label: vertebrate
description: Flowers are observed to be vertebrate-pollinated (bats, birds, mammals or lizards).

label: wasp
description: Flowers are observed to be wasp-pollinated.

label: water
description: Flowers are observed to be water-pollinated.

label: wind
description: Flowers are observed to be wind-pollinated.

label: self
description: Flowers are self-pollinated.

label: apical_buds
description: Plants resprout from above-ground apical meristems. Also termed a caudex. Term refers to palm-like plants with aerial buds that resprout, including grass trees, palms, tree ferns, and pandanus. (Synonyms, aerial_resprouter, apical_resprouter)

label: basal_buds
description: Plants resprout from its base, with buds originating from stem tissue (e.g. lignotuber) and root tissue (root crown) not distinguished between. Most buds designated as being basal are likely to be resprouts from a lignotuber, but this trait value is used if the dataset reported `basal buds` rather than `basal stem buds` or `lignotuber` (Synonyms, coppice).

label: basal_stem_buds
description: Plants resprout from the base of the stem. Australian plants with basal stem buds usually have a lignotuber, documented in the trait `storage_organ`. (Synonyms, rootstock, lignotuber)

label: epicormic_buds
description: Plants resprout from the stem or trunk.

label: fleshy_underground_organ
description: Plants resprouts from buds on a fleshy underground organ that is a taproot tuber, bulb, corm, stem tuber, root tuber, or belowground caudex. (Synonyms, geophyte)

label: root_crown
description: Plants resprout from the root crown, the root tissue at the root-stem transition.

label: bud-bearing_root
description: Root buds produce vertical suckers (from root crown) or adventitious roots. (Synonyms, root-suckering, adventitious_buds)

label: rhizome
description: Plants resprout from buds on a rhizome, where it is not specified if the rhizome is woody or non-woody.

label: rhizome_woody
description: Plants resprout from buds on a woody rhizome.

label: rhizome_non_woody
description: Plants resprout from buds on a fleshy rhizome, rhizophore, or fibrous rhizome.

label: stem_buds
description: Plants resprout from stem buds; this trait value is separate to epicormic buds. (Synonyms, aerial_axillary_resprouter)

label: stem_tuber
description: Plants resprout from buds on a stem tuber.

label: stolon
description: Horizontal branches (stems) resprout from the base of the plant.

label: underground_buds
description: Plants that resprout from underground organ, but the type of organ isn't specified.

label: none
description: Plants lack regenerative buds.

label: bulb
description: Below ground storage organ derived from stem and usually leaf tissue.

label: corm
description: Below ground storage organ that is a short, rounded, vertical, fleshy, underground stem.

label: caudex
description: Swollen stem that usually functions in water storage, although the term can also apply to below ground structures or to swollen roots.

label: fleshy_underground_organ
description: Plants that use fleshy, generally underground organs (swellings) to regenerate, but the type of organ is not specified; examples include corms, tubers, bulbs, and caudex.

label: lignotuber
description: Swollen woody structures are located at the transition between the stem base and root crown of woody shrubs, mallees and small trees, and are formed from stem tissues. Buds are located over the entire structure. No colonisation ability.

label: pseudobulb
description: An above ground storage organ present in many terrestrial and epiphytic orchids created throough the thickening of the stem between leaf nodes.

label: rhizome
description: A type of continually growing or creeping underground stem, but it is not specified if the rhizome is woody or non-woody.

label: rhizome_woody
description: A type of continually growing or creeping woody underground stem.

label: rhizome_fleshy
description: A type of continually growing or creeping fleshy, non-woody underground stem.

label: rhizome_fibrous
description: A type of continually growing or creeping fibrous, non-woody underground stem.

label: root_tuber
description: A swollen root the stores nutrients, carbohydrates and water. (Synonyms, taproot_tuber)

label: stem_tuber
description: A swollen underground stem that stores nutrients, carbohydrates and water.

label: storage_organ
description: Plant has a storage organ, but the type is unknown.

label: tuber
description: A swollen underground organ that stores nutrients, carbohydrates and water, where it is not specified if the tuber develops from root or stem tissue.

label: roots_woody
description: Plants have woody roots.

label: no_storage_organ
description: No storage organ present

label: lignotuber_absent
description: A plant that explicitly lacks a lignotuber.

label: resprouts_non_fire_disturbance
description: Plants have the ability to resprout following a disturbance other than fire that causes 100% leaf loss.

label: resprouts_after_cyclone
description: Plants are able to resprout following 100% leaf loss in a cyclone.

label: resprouts_after_drought
description: Plants are able to resprout following 100% leaf loss during a drought.

label: resprouts_after_non-fire_stem_loss
description: Plants are able to resprout following 100% leaf loss following stem or branch removal.

label: killed_by_non_fire_disturbance
description: Plants do not resprout following a non-fire disturbance that leads to 100% leaf loss.

label: aboveground_clonal
description: Vegetative buds or plant fragments that can disperse and produce new plants (including axillary buds, bulbils and turions).

label: adventitious_roots
description: Adventitious roots can form at nodes on the main roots or aboveground from nodes on stems.

label: bulb
description: Below ground storage organ derived from stem (and sometimes leaf) tissue, that divides into new individuals.

label: belowground_clonal
description: Plants use an unspecified underground organ for clonal spread.

label: corm
description: Below ground organ derived from stem tissue that can function either for vegetative spread or to regenerate following a disturbance.

label: rhizome
description: Plant has an underground stem that has stem buds and forms adventitious roots at nodes; this stem may be woody or non-woody. Rhizomes are both a mechanism for vegetative spread and a strategy to survive fire.

label: root_buds
description: Root buds that produce vertical suckers. (Synonyms, root_suckers)

label: root_tuber
description: A swollen root that functions as a storage organ and has buds that allow clonal growth.

label: stem_tuber
description: A swollen underground stem that functions as a storage organ and has buds that allow clonal growth.

label: stolon
description: Plants having horizontal branches (stems) from the base of the plant that produce new plants from buds at its tip or nodes.

label: viviparous
description: Plant produces clonal offspring that grow while still attached to the parent plant.

label: non_clonal
description: Plant does not display clonal growth.

label: clonal
description: A plant is able to spread clonally, but the mechanism is not specified.

label: stem_suckers
description: Stem buds that produce vertical suckers. (Synonyms, stem_buds, rooting_at_nodes)

label: stolon_absent
description: Plants lack horizontal branches (stems) that produce new plants from buds.

label: type_i
description: The primary root is fibrous or fleshy and is relatively long; mesophytic.

label: type_ii
description: The primary root is relatively short and is fibrous. Roots are well branched in a dry habitat but branch little in one that is wet.

label: type_iii
description: The primary root is usually long and fibrous. The first order lateral roots are well branched and are usually short; they are rather evenly distributed along the primary root; xerophytic.

label: type_iv
description: The primary root is usually long and slender like that of Type II. The first order lateral roots are well branched. Those closest to the surface of the ground, or not far below, are relatively long; xerophytic and mesophytic.

label: type_v
description: The primary root is divided-forked or branched-and fibrous, and with few first order lateral roots, or, in age, apparently with none; xerophytic.

label: type_vi
description: The primary root is usually as in Type V. The first order lateral roots are mostly on the upper portion of the primary root and are thus relatively superficial; xerophytic or in well aerated sandy soil where the rainfall is not light.

label: type_vii
description: Adventitious roots that are in one group and arise on a short horizontal, or vertical, axis of the shoot. They are fibrous or fleshly; mesophytic and hydrophytic.

label: type_viii
description: Adventitious roots that are in one group and are fibrous and fleshy, or fibrous and thick. The fibrous adventitious roots are absorbing-anchoring roots and are usually with laterals to the second order; meophytic.

label: type_ix
description: Adventitious roots that arise on the aerial stem and branches of some herbaceous taxa, shrubs, and trees; on creepers, vines, and runners; and on subterranean rhizomes and stolons.

label: arbuscular_mycorrhizal
description: Symbiosis in which the mycorrhizal fungi does penetrate the cortex cells of the plant roots and its hyphae form arbuscules and vesicles inside the plant root; endomycorrhizal, AM, VAM.

label: carnivorous
description: Plant has non-mycorrhizal carnivorous root.

label: cluster_roots
description: Non-proteoid taxa with cluster roots.

label: coiling_vam
description: Associations that spread predominantly by intracellular hyphal coils within roots.

label: dauciform_root
description: A type of cluster root found in the family Cyperaceae.

label: ectomycorrhizal
description: Symbiosis in which the mycorrhizal fungi does not penetrate the cortex cells of the plant roots.

label: ericoid_mycorrhizal
description: A form of arbuscular mycorrhizal relationship only found on plants in the order Ericales. The fungi's hyphae penetrate the plant root but do not form arbuscules.

label: fine_roots
description: Particularly fine roots for nutrient uptake.

label: haustorium
description: A highly modified stem or root of a parasitic plant, such as mistletoe , or a specialized branch or tube originating from a hairlike filament (hypha) of a fungus. The haustorium penetrates the tissues of a host and absorbs nutrients and water.

label: hemiparasitic_root
description: Plant with a partially parasitic root.

label: long_root_hairs
description: Plant with specialised long root hairs.

label: mycorrhizal
description: Plant mycorrhizal but type not specified.

label: non_mycorrhizal
description: Plants lacking a mycorrhizal symbiont.

label: orchid_mycorrhizal
description: A mycorrhizal relationship specific to orchid taxa, and for most orchids, essential for seedlings to establish.

label: parasitic_root
description: Plant with a parasitic root.

label: proteoid_root
description: Also known as cluster roots, are plant roots that form clusters of closely spaced short lateral rootlets and aid in nutrient upake in nutrient-poor soils; common in members of the family Proteaceae but present in other families as well.

label: root_hairs
description: Plant with specialised root hairs.

label: sand-binding
description: Persistent sheaths of sand that form around the roots of taxa in the families Restionaceae, Cyperaceae, Haemodoraceae, and Lomandraceae in western Australia. Assumed to function in nutrient uptake.

label: saprophyte
description: Plant that acquires nutrients from decaying biomass.

label: subepidermal_mycorrhizal
description: Mycorrhizae where hyphae grow in a cavity under epidermal cells. Only in the genus Thysanotus (family Laxmaniaceae).

label: unknown
description: Root structures unknown.

label: glycophyte
description: Plants that cannot survive even one tenth the salt concentration found in seawater.

label: halophyte
description: Plants that complete their life cycle in a salty environment; many survive in seawater or even higher concentrations of salt.

label: halophyte_moderate
description: Plant that is moderately tolerant of soil salinity/sodicity.

label: hydrohalophyte
description: Tidal swamp or 'mangrove' and coastal lagoon elements and temperate-zone salt-marsh taxa are classed together.

label: salt_spray_tolerant
description: Plant that is tolerant of salt spray (typically inhabiting near-coastal environments).

label: salinity_tolerance_undefined
description: Plant's ability to tolerate salt is unknown.

label: xerohalophyte
description: Plants adapted to inland salt desert and saline habitats.

label: comma-shaped
description: A seed displaying a single arc of curvature, such that it bilaterally symmetrical. (Synonyms, falcate, sickle-shaped, scimitar-shaped)

label: conical
description: Cone-shaped, with a broad flat base and narrow apex; turbinate refers to the inverse shape. (Synonyms, obconical, cone-shaped, turbinate, top-shaped)

label: cuneate
description: A 3-dimensional shape that is wedge-shaped or boat-shaped.

label: cylindrical
description: A cylinder, a shape with a flat top and bottom that are circular or elliptical in outline and are linked by a curved surface. (Synonyms, terete)

label: discoid
description: A subset of cylinder, a shape with a flat, circular or elliptical top and bottom, linked by a curved surface, where the length of the curved surface is much shorter than the cross-section of the flat surfaces. (Synonyms, flat)

label: ellipsoid
description: A 3-dimensional shape that is elliptic in long section and circular in cross section; length:width ratio between 2:1 and 3:2. (Synonyms, obloid, oblong)

label: ellipsoid_flattened
description: A 3-dimensional shape that is elliptic in long section and and laterally compressed/flattened such that it is non-circular in cross section; length:width ratio between 2:1 and 3:2.

label: fusiform
description: Spindle-shaped; A 3-dimension shape that is narrowly ellipsoid, circular in cross-section and tapering sharply toward both ends. (Synonyms, spindle-shaped)

label: globoid
description: A 3-dimensional shape that is circular in both long section and cross section. (Synonyms, globose, globular, spherical)

label: globoid_flattened
description: A 3-dimensional shape that is circular in both long section and somewhat flattened such that it is non-circular in cross section.

label: hemispheric
description: Half a sphere or globe, with a flat base, domed top, and circular in cross-section. (Synonyms, convex)

label: hemispheric_flattened
description: A 3-dimensional shape that is a laterally compressed/flattened half-sphere or globe; shape has a flat base, a domed top, and is elliptical in cross-section.

label: lenticular
description: Shaped like a biconvex lens and circular in cross section; shaped like a lentil.

label: orbicular
description: A poorly defined term that remains in AusTraits only as a placeholder; it appears to be used as both globoid (spherical) and lenticular by different authors.

label: ovoid
description: A 3-dimensional shape that is egg-shaped in long section and circular in cross section. Term as used in AusTraits includes variants on egg-shaped including pyriform (pear-shaped) and obovoid (inversely egg-shaped) (Synonyms, pyriform, obovoid)

label: ovoid_elongated
description: A 3-dimensional shape that is egg-shaped in long section and circular in cross section, where the length dimension is much longer than the width/height dimensions. Term as used in AusTraits includes specific shapes club-shaped (clavate/obclavate) and tear-shaped (lachrimiform). (Synonyms, lachrimiform, tear-shaped, lachrymiform, clavate; obclavate, club-shaped)

label: ovoid_flattened
description: A 3-dimensional shape that is egg-shaped in long section and laterally compressed/flattened such that is non-circular in cross section.

label: polyhedral
description: A 3-dimensional shape with distinct, fairly flat faces and edges; includes prisms and tetrahedral shaped seeds. (Synonyms, rhomboid, prismatic, pyramidal, rectangular, square)

label: polyhedral_elongated
description: A 3-dimensional shape with distinct, fairly flat faces and edges, where the length dimension is much longer than the width/height dimensions; includes elongate prisms and elongate tetrahedral shaped seeds.

label: polyhedral_inflated
description: A 3-dimensional shape with distinct faces and edges but the faces tend to bulge outwards.

label: reniform
description: Having a cross-section that is roughly circular with a notch; strictly a kidney-shape but the definition applied here includes heart-shaped seeds and other seeds with a distinct notch. (Synonyms, cordiform, kidney-shaped, heart-shaped)

label: winged
description: A seed with wings. (Synonyms, samara)

label: sectoroid
description: Shaped like an orange segment or wedge of a sphere. (Synonyms, wedge-shaped)

label: sinusoidal
description: A seed with two arcs of curvature or a single arc, such that it lacks an axis of symmetry. (Synonyms, sigmoidal)

label: glabrous
description: Seed surface lacks trichomes or bristles.

label: hairs
description: Seed surface with trichomes or bristles.

label: hairs_branched
description: Seed surface with branched trichomes or bristles.(Synonyms, stellate, plumose)

label: hairs_simple
description: Seed surface with simple trichomes or bristles. (Synonyms, tomentose, velutinous, velvety, sericeous)

label: dull
description: Seed surface appears dull, indicating it has a low reflectivity.

label: shiny
description: Seed surface appears shiny or glossy, indicating it has a high reflectivity. (Synonyms, glossy, lustrous, polished)

label: bumpy
description: Seed surface covered with minute, rounded protuberances. (Synonyms, colliculate, verrucate, papillate, tuberculate, undulate)

label: grooved
description: Seed surface covered with grooves.

label: netted
description: Seed surface covered with raised, reticulate, interconnected ridges. (Synonyms, reticulate, honey-combed)

label: papery
description: Seed surface with a thin and papery texture. (Synonyms, chartaceous)

label: pitted
description: Seed surface pitted. (Synonyms, foveolate, foveate, dimpled, punctate, lacunose)

label: ribbed
description: Seed surface with longitudinal raised ribs or ridges. (Synonyms, costate, carinate, lineate, fluted, striate, strigose, lineolate, scalariform, ridged)

label: rough
description: Seed surface rough with no organisation of markings, resembling sandpaper. (Synonyms, scabrous)

label: scaly
description: Seed surface rough with loose scales differing in direction or not parallel in direction. (Synonyms, scurfy, squarrose)

label: smooth
description: Seed surface smooth, lacking texture. (Synonyms, glabrous)

label: spiny
description: Seed surface with spines. (Synonyms, echinulate)

label: wrinkled
description: Seed surface with a wrinkled, rugose texture. (Synonyms, rugose, rugulose, bullate)

label: seedbank
description: A seedbank exists, but its locations is not specified.

label: canopy_seedbank
description: Seeds stored in the canopy, usually still within a woody cone.

label: soil_seedbank
description: Seeds stored in the soil.

label: canopy_seedbank_absent
description: Seed explicitly not stored in the canopy.

label: soil_seedbank_absent
description: Seed explicitly not stored in the soil.

label: none
description: Seeds are not stored.

label: transient
description: Seed that survives in the seedbank until its first annual germination season, but not until its second annual germination season. Some transient seeds will germinate within weeks to months, while others may remain in the seedbank for slightly over a year, depending on how the annual recruitment season aligns with seed maturation. Transient seeds are non-dormant, remaining in the seedbank until environmental conditions are appropriate for germination.

label: persistent
description: Seed that survives in the seedbank until at least its second germination season.

label: short_persistent
description: Seed that persists in the seedbank for approximately 1 to 5 years, although the time interval varies by study.

label: long_persistent
description: Seed that persists in the seedbank for more than 5 years, although the time interval varies by study.

label: widely_dispersed
description: Seed longevity not important, as seeds are widely dispersed and always available for germination.

label: not_serotinous
description: Plant does not display serotiny.

label: serotinous
description: Plant serotinous, level not specified.

label: serotiny_low
description: Plant displays a weak level of serotiny, indicating it releases most of its seeds gradually, with only a small proportion of the seeds retained as a canopy seedbank until an environmental cue triggers the release of the entire seedbank.

label: serotiny_moderate
description: Plant displays a moderate level of serotiny, indicating it releases some of its seeds gradually, with the remainder retained as a canopy seedbank until an environmental cue triggers the release of the entire seedbank.

label: serotiny_high
description: Plant displays a strong level of serotiny, indicating all seeds are retained as a canopy seedbank until an environmental cue triggers their release.

label: scale-like
description: The leaf at the first stem node above the epicotyl is scale-like, also referred to as a cataphyll.

label: leaf-like
description: The leaf at the first stem node above the epicotyl is leaf-like (broad).

label: single
description: There is a single leaf at the first stem node above the epicotyl.

label: paired
description: There is a pair of leaves at the first stem node above the epicotyl.

label: not_applicable
description: Taxa is virtually never confronted with snow in nature and the response is unknown.

label: intolerant
description: Taxa is frost tender and known to be killed by any snow.

label: days
description: Taxa can tolerate being covered by snow for days (typically less than 1 week).

label: weeks
description: Taxa can tolerate being covered by snow for weeks (typically less than 1 month).

label: months
description: Taxa can tolerate being covered by snow for months.

label: absent
description: Plant that lacks a physical defence structure.

label: sharp_pointed_defence
description: Plant that has either spines, thorns, or prickles but the type of physical defence structure is not specified.

label: prickle
description: A sharp-tipped outgrowth from the epidermis, bark or other plant organ that is explicitly not a spine (modified leaf) or thorn (modified stem).

label: pungent_leaf_apex
description: A sharp-tipped leaf.

label: spine
description: A sharp-pointed structure, which is a modified leaf or leaf part, including petioles, midribs, secondary veins, leaflets, or stipules.

label: stinging_or_irritant_hairs
description: Trichomes that sting or irritate, by injecting a toxin.

label: thorn
description: A sharp-pointed, stiff, woody modified stem.

label: subspinescent
description: A plant bearing weakly or partially developed spine-like structures.

label: no_spines
description: No spines. (level 0)

label: low_density_soft_spines
description: Low or very local density of soft spines <5mm long; plant may sting or prickle when hit carelessly but not impart strong pain. (level 1)

label: high_density_soft_spines
description: High density of soft spines, intermediate density of spines of intermediate hardness, or low density of hard, sharp spines >5mm long; plant causes actual pain when hit carelessly. (level 2)

label: high_density_hard_spines_to_5mm
description: Intermediate or high density of hard, sharp spines >5mm long; plant causes strong pain when hit carelessly. (level 3)

label: high_density_hard_spines_to_20mm
description: Intermediate or high density of hard, sharp spines >20mm long; plant may cause significant wounds when hit carelessly. (level 4)

label: high_density_hard_spines_to_100mm
description: Intermediate or high density of hard, sharp spines >100mm long; plant is dangerous to careless large mammals, including humans. (level 5)

label: amphistomatic
description: Leaves with stomata on both leaf surfaces.

label: amphistomatic_uneven
description: Leaves with stomata on both leaf surfaces but more stomata on the lower leaf surface.

label: epistomatic
description: Leaves that only have stomata on the upper (adaxial) leaf surface.

label: hypostomatic
description: Leaves that only have stomata on the lower (abaxial) leaf surface.

label: stomata_covered_with_dense_hairs
description: Stomata densely covered by hairs.

label: stomata_not_covered_by_hairs
description: Stomata not hair-covered.

label: taproot
description: Taproot, where the primary root remains dominant and grows downward as a single thick main root.

label: taproot_absent
description: Tap root not present.

label: taproot_sometimes_present
description: Tap root sometimes present.

label: taproot_slender
description: Slender, thin taproot.

label: taproot_stout
description: Stout, thick, robust taproot.

label: taproot_fleshy
description: Fleshy, swollen taproot.

label: taproot_branched
description: Taproot that bears prominent lateral branches.

label: taproot_unbranched
description: Unbranched taproot.

label: aquatic_rooted
description: Aquatic plant that is rooted in the substrate rather than free-floating.

label: adventitious_roots
description: Adventitious roots, which arise from stems, leaves, or other tissues rather than from the primary root.

label: coralloid_roots
description: Coralloid roots, short, branched, coral-like roots.

label: sand-binding_roots
description: Sand-binding roots, which are sheathed in sand grains held in place by root hairs and mucilage.

label: stilt_roots
description: Stilt roots, adventitious roots that arise from the lower stem and reach the ground, providing additional support.

label: stilt_roots_absent
description: A plant that explicitly lacks stilt roots.

label: prop_roots
description: Prop roots, adventitious roots that arise from the stem above ground and brace the plant.

label: prop_roots_absent
description: A plant that explicitly lacks prop roots.

label: aerial_roots
description: Aerial roots, roots that grow above the ground or water surface.

label: aerial_roots_absent
description: A plant that explicitly lacks aerial roots.

label: fibrous_roots
description: A fibrous root system, in which many roots of similar size arise.

label: fleshy_roots
description: Fleshy, thickened roots that store water or nutrients.

label: napiform_roots
description: Napiform (turnip-shaped) roots, swollen and rounded above and tapering abruptly below.

label: non-tuberous_roots
description: A plant whose roots are not swollen into storage tubers.

label: deep_rooted
description: Deep root system that extends well below the soil surface.

label: shallow_rooted
description: Shallow root system concentrated near the soil surface.

label: not_vegetative
description: Plant taxa that regenerate and spread only by seed.

label: vegetative
description: Plant taxa that can regenerate and spread through the growth and division of vegetative material, not just from seed; examples include runners, rhizomes, and bulbs.

label: vegetative_obligate
description: Plant taxa that never (or very rarely) regenerate from seed, instead regenerating and spreading entirely through the growth and division of vegetative material.

label: not_applicable
description: Taxa is not typically confronted with waterlogging and its response is unknown.

label: less_than_1_month
description: Taxa able to tolerate less than 1 month of waterlogging.

label: 1-6_months
description: Taxa able to tolerate 1-6 months of waterlogging.

label: greater_than_6_months
description: Taxa able to tolerate more than 6 months of waterlogging.

label: aquatic
description: Taxa truly aquatic and able to be permanently inundated.

label: herbaceous
description: Plant with non-lignified stems.

label: woody
description: Plant whose stems are stiff and lignified, including both stems that produce secondary xylem and those that produce only lignified primary tissues but are notably stiff and robust.

label: herbaceous
description: Plant with non-lignified stems.

label: woody
description: Plant whose stems produce secondary xylem (true wood).

label: woody_base
description: Plant where secondary xylem (true wood) is present only at the base of stems. (Synonyms, suffrutescent)

label: woody_root
description: Plant that has a woody rootstock but non-woody above-ground stems.

label: semi_woody
description: Plant that forms stems considered only "partially woody", generally having lower lignin and cellulose contents and possibly not forming secondary xylem. These are generally short-lived, fast-growing stems. (Synonyms, green-stem_shrub, soft_shrub, soft_wood)

label: woody_like_stem
description: Taxa, including monocots and ferns, that produce thick, stiff, robust lignified stems but do not produce secondary xylem.

label: woody_like_inflorescence
description: Taxa, including monocots, that produce thick, stiff, robust lignified inflorescence shoots but are otherwise non-woody.

label: blue_purple
description: Seed coat is blue to purple.

label: green

description: Seed coat is red to brown.

label: cord_roots
description: A root anatomy found within three genera of Mirbelieae (Daviesia, Euchilopsis, Phyllota) wherein networks of interlinking vascular strands exist (Crisp 2003; Pate and Dixon 1996).

label: unistelar_roots
description: The commonly observed root anatomy, wherein there is a single vascular strand which displays secondary thickening.

label: leafless
description: A leafless plant, which lacks leaves and therefore has no leaf length to record.

label: compound
description: A plant with compound leaves, for which leaflet_length, not leaf_length, is the appropriate trait under which to record the maximum length of the leaf unit.

label: bladeless
description: A plant whose leaves lack a distinct blade (lamina), such that leaf_length is not the appropriate trait under which to record leaf dimensions.

label: scale_leaves
description: A plant with scale leaves, such that leaf_length is not the appropriate trait under which to record leaf dimensions. (Synonyms, na_reduced_to_scales)

label: reduced
description: A plant whose leaves are reduced, such that leaf_length is not the appropriate trait under which to record leaf dimensions, but their form is not specified.

label: reduced_to_sheath
description: A plant whose leaves are reduced to a sheath, such that leaf_length is not the appropriate trait under which to record leaf dimensions.

label: not_given
description: A leaf length was not given in the data source consulted.

label: not_given_flora
description: A leaf length was not given in the flora consulted.

label: not_given_taxon_description
description: A leaf length was not given in the taxon description consulted.

label: aquatic
description: An aquatic plant, which may be submerged or floating, but which is not self-supporting and therefore stem_length, not plant_height, is the appropriate trait under which to record the length of the vegetative shoot system.

label: aquatic_floating
description: A floating aquatic plant for which stem_length, not plant_height, is the appropriate trait under which to record the length of the vegetative shoot system.

label: aquatic_submerged
description: A submerged aquatic plant for which stem_length, not plant_height, is the appropriate trait under which to record the length of the vegetative shoot system.

label: climbing
description: A climbing plant, which is not self-supporting and therefore stem_length or plant_height_climbing, not plant_height, is the appropriate trait under which to record the length of the vegetative shoot system.

label: epiphyte
description: An epiphyte, which is not rooted in soil and therefore stem_length, not plant_height, is the appropriate trait under which to record the length of the vegetative shoot system.

label: geophyte
description: A geophyte, which lacks a permanent aboveground shoot system, such that the height of the reproductive shoot system (plant_height_reproductive) is the appropriate trait under which to record the maximum height of the plant.

label: lithophyte
description: A lithophyte, which grows on the surface of rocks rather than rooted in soil, and therefore stem_length, not plant_height, is the appropriate trait under which to record the length of the vegetative shoot system.

label: mat-forming
description: A mat-forming plant, which is a low-growing plant with prostrate stems that root at the nodes, and while it will have a height of a few cm, plant_width or stem_length are often the only plant dimensions reported. (Synonyms, na_cushion)

label: marine
description: A marine plant, which grows submerged in seawater and is not self-supporting, and therefore stem_length, not plant_height, is the appropriate trait under which to record the length of the vegetative shoot system.

label: rosette
description: A plant whose leaves are arranged in a ring (rosette) on the ground surface and only has a flowering stem that elongates, such that plant_height_reproductive, not plant_height, is the appropriate trait under which to record the maximum height of the plant.

label: leaf_tuft
description: A plant whose leaves are arranged in a tuft on the ground surface and only has a flowering stem that elongates, such that plant_height_reproductive, not plant_height, is the appropriate trait under which to record the maximum height of the plant.

label: prostrate
description: A prostrate plant, whose stems grow along the ground surface, generally rising just slightly, and therefore stem_length, gives a better indication of the length of the vegetative shoot system than does plant_height, although both maybe recorded. (Synonyms, na_trailing, na_creeping, na_decumbent)

label: rhizome
description: A plant whose main stem is a horizontal rhizome, and therefore stem_length, not plant_height, is the appropriate trait under which to record the length of the vegetative shoot system.

description: A plant height was not given in the taxon description consulted.

label: stipule_absent
description: Leaves lack stipules. (Synonyms, exstipulate)

label: acuminate
description: Leaf apex has a long, narrow, tapering point.

label: acute
description: Leaf apex comes to a point at an angle of less than 90 degrees.

label: obtuse
description: Leaf apex comes to a point at an angle of more than 90 degrees.

label: rounded

label: apiculate
description: Leaf apex narrows abruptly to a small, sharp terminal point (a mucro). (Synonyms, mucro)

label: petiole_present
description: Leaves have a petiole. (Synonyms, petiolate).

label: petiole_absent
description: Leaves lack a petiole and attach directly to the stem. (Synonyms, sessile)

label: decurrent
description: Petiole with a winged extension that extends down the stem. (Synonyms, winged, clasping)

label: not_decurrent
description: Petiole without a winged extension that extends down the stem.

label: slender
description: Petiole that is long and thin.

label: glaucous
description: Juvenile phase leaves have a waxy coating, giving them a glaucous appearance. (Synonyms, waxy_bloom, pruinose)

label: not_glaucous
description: Juvenile phase leaves do not have a glaucous appearance. (Synonyms, green)

label: subglaucous
description: Juvenile phase leaves have a thin or patchy waxy coating, giving them a slightly glaucous appearance intermediate between glaucous and not glaucous. (Synonyms, semi-glaucous)

label: amorphous
description: Epicuticular wax forms a continuous amorphous film without distinct crystals. (Synonyms, wax_film)

label: granules
description: Epicuticular wax crystals are small irregular granules.

label: plates
description: Epicuticular wax crystals are flat plates (platelets), with entire, sinuate, crenate or digitate edges. (Synonyms, platelets)

label: tubes
description: Epicuticular wax crystals are hollow tubes (tubules), simple or branched. (Synonyms, tubules)

label: low

label: open

label: sunken
description: Stomata recessed below the general level of the epidermal surface, in shallow pits or below a raised cuticular rim or papillae, but not deeply enough to be encrypted.

label: superficial
description: Stomata level with the epidermal surface, or only weakly recessed.

label: actinocytic
description: Stomata surrounded by a ring of radially elongated subsidiary cells.

label: anisocytic
description: Stomata surrounded by three subsidiary cells, one distinctly smaller than the other two.

label: anomocytic
description: Stomata surrounded by a variable number of cells that are not distinguishable from other epidermal cells (no distinct subsidiary cells).

label: cyclocytic
description: Stomata surrounded by one or two narrow rings of four or more subsidiary cells.

label: diacytic
description: Stomata enclosed by a pair of subsidiary cells whose common walls are at right angles to the guard cells.

label: paracytic
description: Stomata accompanied on either side by one or more subsidiary cells whose long axes are parallel to the guard cells.

label: tetracytic
description: Stomata surrounded by four subsidiary cells, two lateral and two polar.

label: smooth

label: rough
description: Bark surface is rough, with irregular cracks, ridges or a coarse texture, but without deep regular furrows.

label: furrowed
description: Bark is thick, with deep longitudinal furrows or fissures separating ridges or plates. (Synonyms, fissured, deeply_fissured)

label: tessellated
description: Bark is broken into small, roughly square or rectangular blocks or plates, forming a tessellated or chequered pattern.

label: fibrous
description: Bark is composed of matted, shortish fibres that come away in soft, spongy or fibrous pieces.

label: stringy

label: constricted

label: connate

label: free

description: Flower has a bilateral asymmetrical shape, with different shaped upper- and lower- lips.

label: campanulate
description: Flower is bell-shaped. (Synonyms, bell-shaped)

label: cup-shaped

label: urceolate
description: Flower is a tube that is narrow at the base and tip and swollen or rounded in the middle. (Synonyms, urn-shaped).

label: acicular
description: Style needle-like. (Synonyms, linear)

label: bilobed

label: clavate
description: Style club-shaped, widening towards the apex. (Synonyms, club-shaped)

label: conical

label: curved

label: filiform

label: flattened

label: fusiform
description: Style spindle-shaped, widest in the middle and tapering to both ends.

label: hemispheric

label: lobed

label: obconical
description: Style inversely cone-shaped, broadest at the apex.

label: ovoid
description: Style swollen and egg-shaped.

label: quadrangular
description: Style four-angled in cross section.

label: subulate
description: Style awl-shaped, tapering from the base to a fine point.

label: terete

label: perianth_parts_unfused

label: perianth_parts_fused_at_base

label: perianth_parts_partially_fused
description: A flower's perianth parts are fused 20-80%, forming a tube, but with the tips free.

label: perianth_tubular
description: A flower's perianth parts are fused >80%, forming a tube.

label: adnate
description: Petals are fused to another floral organ, such as the stamens or the hypanthium.

label: connate
description: Petals are fused to one another, forming a corolla tube or cup. (Synonyms, united, gamopetalous, sympetalous)

label: free
description: Petals are free from one another. (Synonyms, polypetalous, choripetalous)

label: bilobed
description: Petal divided at the apex into two lobes. (Synonyms, bifid, 2-lobed)

label: boat-shaped
description: Petal concave and keeled, like the hull of a boat. (Synonyms, cymbiform, navicular)

label: cordate
description: A 2-dimensional heart shape, approximately ovate with a cordate base, with the point of attachment at the notch between the lobes. (Synonyms, cordiform)

label: elliptical
description: A 2-dimensional shape that is an oval, with curved margins, lacking a distinct point, and a length:width ratio between 2:1 and 3:2. (Synonyms, oval)

label: falcate
description: A 2-dimensional sickle-shape, approximately lanceolate to linear and curved on one side. (Synonyms, scimitar-shaped, sickle-shaped, falciform, crescent-shaped, crescentic)

label: filiform
description: A 2-dimensional shape that is long, thin, and typically flexuous, threadlike, filamentous. (Synonyms, capillary)

label: hastate
description: Petal approximately triangular with two outward-pointing basal lobes, like an arrowhead with flared barbs.

label: hooded
description: Petal concave and arched over at the apex, forming a hood. (Synonyms, cucullate)

label: lanceolate
description: A 2-dimensional shape that is narrowly egg-shaped or teardrop-shaped, with a length:width ratio between 6:1 and 3:1. The petal is widest below the middle, towards its base.

label: linear
description: A 2-dimensional shape that is very long and narrow, has parallel sides and a length:width ratio between 12:1 and 6:1.

label: lobed
description: Petal divided into lobes; the number of lobes not specified or more than three.

label: oblanceolate
description: A 2-dimensional shape that is narrowly teardrop-shaped, with a length:width ratio between 6:1 and 3:1, widest above the middle and tapering towards the base.

label: oblong
description: A 2-dimensional shape that is somewhat elongated with parallel sides and a length:width ratio between 2:1 and 3:2.

label: obovate
description: A 2-dimensional shape that is egg-shaped, with a length:width ratio between 2:1 and 3:2, widest above the middle and tapering towards the base.

label: orbicular
description: A 2-dimensional shape that is approximately circular. (Synonyms, circular)

label: ovate
description: A 2-dimensional shape that is egg-shaped, with a length:width ratio between 2:1 and 3:2. The petal is widest below the middle, towards its base.

label: reniform
description: A 2-dimensional shape that is roughly kidney-shaped, wider than long with a rounded apex and two rounded, basal lobes that are smoothly concave at their intersection. (Synonyms, kidney-shaped)

label: rhomboidal
description: A 2-dimensional shape that is approximately diamond or parallelogram-shaped, with approximately straight edges, widest near the middle, and a length:width ratio 2:1 to 3:2. The petal is attached at one of the points.

label: saccate
description: Petal with a pouch-like swelling. (Synonyms, pouched, gibbous)

label: semicircular
description: Petal approximately half-circular in outline.

label: spathulate
description: A 2-dimensional shape that can be approximately oblong, obovate, or oblanceolate in outline with a long attenuate base, like a spoon. (Synonyms, spoon-shaped, clavate)

label: subulate
description: A 2-dimensional shape that is awl-shaped, approximately narrowly oblong to narrowly triangular with a broad base. (Synonyms, awl-shaped)

label: triangular
description: A 2-dimensional shape that is triangular to wedge-shaped, with a length:width ratio 2:1 to 3:2 and widest at the base.

label: trilobed
description: Petal divided at the apex into three lobes. (Synonyms, trifid, 3-lobed)

label: adnate
description: Sepals are fused to another floral organ.

label: connate
description: Sepals are fused to one another. (Synonyms, united, fused, joined)

label: free
description: Sepals are free from one another.

label: clavate
description: Fruit is club-shaped, elongate and gradually widening towards the apex.

label: coiled
description: Fruit is coiled through one or more turns. (Synonyms, circinnate, spiral, spirally_twisted)

label: conical
description: Fruit is cone-shaped, broadest at the base and narrowing to the apex.

label: constricted
description: Fruit is elongate and constricted between the seeds.

label: cup-shaped
description: Fruit is cup-shaped, open or flattened at the apex with convex sides. (Synonyms, cupular, cupuliform)

label: curved
description: Fruit is elongate and curved along its length. (Synonyms, arcuate, falcate, recurved, sigmoid)

label: cylindrical
description: Fruit is a cylinder, circular in cross section with parallel sides. (Synonyms, terete, barrel-shaped, doliiform)

label: ellipsoid
description: Fruit is elliptic in long section and circular in cross section, with curved sides; length:width ratio between 2:1 and 3:2.

label: flattened
description: Fruit is laterally compressed, non-circular in cross section. (Synonyms, compressed, flat)

label: fusiform
description: Fruit is spindle-shaped, narrowly ellipsoid and tapering towards both ends. (Synonyms, spindle-shaped)

label: globoid
description: Fruit is circular in both long section and cross section. (Synonyms, globose, globular, spherical)

label: hemispheric
description: Fruit is half a sphere, with a flat base and a domed top. (Synonyms, hemispherical)

label: lenticular
description: Fruit is shaped like a biconvex lens and circular in outline.

label: linear
description: Fruit is very long and narrow with parallel sides, such as many legume pods.

label: moniliform
description: Fruit is elongate and deeply constricted between the seeds, like a string of beads.

label: obconical
description: Fruit is inversely cone-shaped, broadest at the apex and narrowing to the base. (Synonyms, turbinate, top-shaped)

label: oblong
description: Fruit is elongate with parallel sides and rounded ends; length:width ratio between 2:1 and 3:2.

label: obovoid
description: Fruit is inversely egg-shaped, broadest above the middle (towards the apex). (Synonyms, pyriform)

label: ovoid
description: Fruit is egg-shaped, broadest below the middle (towards the base).

label: reniform
description: Fruit is kidney-shaped, with a notch on one side.

label: straight
description: Fruit is elongate and straight along its length.

label: twisted
description: Fruit is twisted about its long axis. (Synonyms, contorted)

label: bumpy
description: Fruit surface covered with small, rounded protuberances. (Synonyms, papillose, tuberculate, verrucose, colliculate)

label: grooved
description: Fruit surface with grooves or furrows. (Synonyms, sulcate)

label: keeled
description: Fruit surface with one or more prominent, sharp ridges (keels).

label: lenticellate
description: Fruit surface dotted with lenticels, small raised pores.

label: netted
description: Fruit surface covered with raised, reticulate, interconnected ridges. (Synonyms, reticulate)

label: pitted
description: Fruit surface pitted. (Synonyms, foveolate, punctate)

label: ribbed
description: Fruit surface with longitudinal raised ribs or ridges. (Synonyms, costate, striate, ridged)

label: rough
description: Fruit surface rough with no organisation of markings. (Synonyms, scabrous)

label: scaly
description: Fruit surface covered with scales.

label: smooth
description: Fruit surface smooth, lacking texture.

label: spiny
description: Fruit surface with spines or short, sharp points. (Synonyms, echinate, muricate, prickly)

label: wrinkled
description: Fruit surface wrinkled. (Synonyms, rugose, rugulose)

label: dull
description: Fruit surface appears dull, with low reflectivity. (Synonyms, matt)

label: glaucous
description: Fruit surface is covered with a whitish or bluish waxy bloom. (Synonyms, pruinose)

label: shiny
description: Fruit surface appears shiny or glossy, with a high reflectivity. (Synonyms, glossy, lustrous)

label: cartilaginous
description: Fruit wall tough and firm but flexible, like cartilage.

label: chartaceous
description: Fruit wall thin and papery. (Synonyms, papery, papyraceous)

label: coriaceous
description: Fruit wall thick, tough and leathery. (Synonyms, leathery, subcoriaceous)

label: corky
description: Fruit wall corky.

label: fibrous
description: Fruit wall fibrous.

label: fleshy
description: Fruit wall soft and juicy. (Synonyms, succulent, subfleshy)

label: hard
description: Fruit wall hard and brittle. (Synonyms, crustaceous, bony, stony)

label: hyaline
description: Fruit wall thin and translucent.

label: membranous
description: Fruit wall very thin and soft. (Synonyms, membranaceous, sub-membranous)

label: rigid
description: Fruit wall stiff.

label: spongy
description: Fruit wall soft and spongy.

label: woody
description: Fruit wall hard and woody. (Synonyms, lignified, subwoody)

label: greater_than_45_degrees
description: Secondary veins diverge from the midrib at an angle greater than 45°. (Synonyms, wide_angle, penniveined)

label: less_than_45_degrees
description: Secondary veins diverge from the midrib at an angle less than 45°. (Synonyms, acute)

label: parallel
description: Secondary veins run approximately parallel to the midrib. (Synonyms, subparallel)

label: perpendicular
description: Secondary veins diverge from the midrib at approximately 90°.

label: intramarginal_vein_present
description: Leaf lamina has an intramarginal vein.

label: intramarginal_vein_absent
description: Leaf lamina lacks an intramarginal vein.

label: close_to_margin
description: Intramarginal vein runs close to the margin.

label: remote_from_margin
description: Intramarginal vein runs well within the margin.

label: diffuse-porous
description: Vessels of more or less uniform diameter throughout the growth ring.

label: ring-porous
description: Vessels in the earlywood distinctly larger than those in the latewood, forming a well-defined zone or ring.

label: semi-ring-porous
description: Vessels in the earlywood larger than those in the latewood, with a gradual change from wide earlywood to narrow latewood vessels.

label: vessel_solitary
description: 90% or more of vessels solitary, not contacting other vessels.

label: vessel_clusters
description: Groups of three or more vessels that contact in both radial and tangential directions is common.

label: vessel_radial_multiples_many
description: Vessels primarily in radial multiples of four or more vessels.

label: vessel_radial_multiples_few
description: Vessels primarily in radial multiples or groups of two or three.

label: foraminate
description: Perforation plate with several more or less circular perforations.

label: reticulate
description: Perforation plate with a net-like pattern of perforations.

label: scalariform
description: Perforation plate with elongated, parallel perforations separated by bars.

label: simple
description: Perforation plate with a single, large, more or less circular perforation.

label: heterocellular
description: Rays composed of cells of different shapes.

label: homocellular
description: All ray cells have the same shape.

label: absent
description: Growth ring boundaries not visible.

label: distinct
description: Growth rings with an abrupt structural change at the boundaries between growth rings.

label: indistinct
description: Growth ring boundaries vague and poorly defined, marked by gradual structural changes.

label: indistinct_or_absent
description: Growth rings vague with their boundaries poorly defined or not visible. Used where a source does not distinguish indistinct from absent growth rings.

label: moderately_distinct
description: Growth ring boundaries evident, but less sharply marked than distinct boundaries.

label: alternate
description: Intervessel pits arranged in diagonal rows.

label: opposite
description: Intervessel pits arranged in short to long horizontal rows, orientated transversely across the length of the vessel.

label: scalariform
description: Elongated or linear intervessel pits arranged in a ladder-like series.

label: not_vestured
description: Intervessel pits without vestures.

label: vestured
description: Intervessel pits with the pit cavity and/or aperture wholly or partly lined with projections from the secondary cell wall.

label: thick-walled
description: Double fibre wall thickness equal to or greater than the width of the fibre lumen, with the lumina still distinctly open.

label: thin-walled
description: Fibre lumina wider than the double wall thickness, but less than three times the double wall thickness.

label: thin_to_thick-walled
description: Fibre lumina less than three times the double wall thickness, and distinctly open. Used where a source does not distinguish thin-walled from thick-walled fibres.

label: very_thick-walled
description: Fibre lumina almost completely closed.

label: very_thin-walled
description: Fibre lumina three or more times wider than the double wall thickness.

label: aliform
description: Parenchyma surrounding or to one side of the vessel, with lateral extensions.

label: confluent
description: Coalescing vasicentric or aliform parenchyma surrounding or to one side of two or more vessels, often forming irregular bands.

label: diffuse
description: Single axial parenchyma strands or pairs of strands distributed irregularly among the fibres.

label: diffuse-in-aggregates
description: Axial parenchyma strands grouped into short, discontinuous tangential or oblique lines.

label: lozenge-aliform
description: Aliform parenchyma with lateral extensions forming a diamond-shaped outline.

label: scanty_paratracheal
description: Occasional parenchyma cells associated with the vessels, or an incomplete sheath of parenchyma around the vessels.

label: unilateral_paratracheal
description: Paratracheal parenchyma forming semicircular hoods or caps only on one side of the vessels.

label: vasicentric
description: Parenchyma cells forming a complete circular to oval sheath around a solitary vessel or vessel multiple.

label: winged-aliform
description: Aliform parenchyma with elongated, narrow lateral extensions.

label: distinctly_bordered
description: Fibre pits with a distinct border, the pit chamber 3 um or more in diameter.

label: moderately_distinctly_bordered
description: Fibre pits with a border that is visible but less distinct than in distinctly bordered pits.

label: simple_to_minutely_bordered
description: Fibre pits simple or with a minute border, the pit chamber less than 3 um in diameter.

label: abundant
description: Wood deposits abundant, filling many cells.

label: absent
description: Wood deposits not seen.

label: moderately_abundant
description: Wood deposits moderately abundant.

label: sparse
description: Wood deposits present in a few cells.

label: unbranched
description: A single stem that does not branch, including references to fern rhizomes. (Synonyms, single-stemmed)

label: branched
description: A plant whose stem divides into branches.

label: few-stemmed
description: A plant with a few stems.

label: multi-stemmed
description: A plant with several stems. (Synonyms, multiple_stems, several-stemmed)

label: many-stemmed
description: A plant with numerous stems.

label: single_basal_stem
description: A plant with a single stem at ground level.

label: multiple_basal_stems
description: A plant with multiple stems arising at ground level.

label: multiple_near_basal_stems
description: A plant with multiple stems arising a little above ground level.

label: much-branched
description: A plant with many branches. (Synonyms, many-branched, twiggy)

label: openly-branched
description: A plant with widely spaced branches. (Synonyms, widely-branched, diffuse)

label: sparsely-branched
description: A plant with few branches. (Synonyms, little-branched, sparingly-branched, few-branched)

label: moderately-branched
description: A plant with an intermediate number of branches.

label: compactly-branched
description: A plant with closely spaced, tightly arranged branches.

label: densely-branched
description: A plant with a high density of branches.

label: intricately-branched
description: A plant with complex, finely divided branching.

label: monopodial
description: A plant with a single main axis bearing lateral branches.

label: horizontally-branched
description: A plant with branches that extend horizontally.

label: tangled
description: A plant with branches that interlace in a disordered manner.

label: gnarled
description: A plant with crooked, twisted, knotty branches.

label: divaricately-branched
description: A plant with branches that diverge at wide angles.

label: dichasially-branched
description: A plant that branches into opposite pairs of lateral axes below each terminal. (Synonyms, corymbose-branched)

label: virgate
description: A plant composed of straight, slender, wand-like stems. (Synonyms, wand-like)

label: buttressed
description: A stem that has a flared shape at its base.

label: fluted
description: A stem with vertical grooves and ridges along its base.

label: rigid
description: Stems that are stiff and resist bending. (Synonyms, stiff)

label: robust
description: Stems that are thick, strong, and sturdy. (Synonyms, stout, sturdy)

label: wiry
description: Stems that are thin but tough and springy.

label: slender
description: Stems that are long and thin. (Synonyms, filiform)

label: straggly
description: Stems that are long, weak, and untidy in arrangement.

label: flexible
description: Stems that bend readily without breaking. (Synonyms, soft, flaccid)

label: wispy
description: Stems that are very fine, thin, and delicate.

label: spindly
description: Plants with weak, skinny branches. (Synonyms, delicate, weak-stemmed)

label: angular
description: Stem angled in cross section. (Synonyms, angled, quadrangular, square, 4-angled, tetragonal, 3-angled, 6-angled)

label: flattened
description: Stem flattened in cross section. (Synonyms, compressed)

label: terete
description: Stem circular in cross section. (Synonyms, subterete, cylindrical)

label: winged
description: Stem with longitudinal wings.

label: broom-like
description: A canopy of many slender, erect branches clustered together like the bristles of a broom.

label: columnar
description: A tall, narrow canopy of roughly uniform width from base to top, with near-vertical sides. (Synonyms, slender)

label: dense-crowned
description: A canopy whose branches and foliage are closely spaced, admitting little light.

label: diffuse
description: A loose, open canopy of widely spaced branches and foliage with an indistinct outline.

label: flat-topped
description: A canopy that is broad and level across the top.

label: globose
description: An approximately spherical canopy, rounded both above and below.

label: hemispherical
description: A canopy shaped like half a sphere, rounded above and flat below. (Synonyms, domed)

label: obconical
description: A canopy shaped like an inverted cone, narrow at the base and broadening upwards, like a spinning top. (Synonyms, top-shaped, turbinate)

label: open-crowned
description: A canopy whose branches and foliage are widely spaced, admitting considerable light.

label: mounded
description: A low, rounded canopy resembling a mound.

label: pine-like
description: A conical canopy of whorled branches tapering to a narrow apex, as in a typical conifer.

label: pyramidal
description: A canopy that is broadest at the base and tapers to a point, triangular in outline.

label: rounded
description: A canopy with a curved, dome-like upper outline.

label: spreading
description: A broad, umbrella-shaped canopy whose branches extend widely outwards, much wider than the trunk. (Synonyms, umbrageous)

label: squat
description: A low, broad canopy that is wider than it is tall. (Synonyms, stunted)

label: woody
description: A woody rhizome.

label: stout

label: branched
description: A branched rhizome.

label: slender

label: short_creeping
description: A short-creeping rhizome that spreads only a short distance horizontally.

label: long_creeping
description: A long-creeping rhizome that spreads a considerable distance horizontally.

label: isophyllous
description: A plant on which all leaves are of a uniform shape and size.

label: anisophyllous
description: A plant that bears leaves of two or more distinctly different shapes or sizes, at a single node, along a shoot, or across developmental stages or environments.

label: arbuscular_mycorrhizal
description: Symbiosis in which the mycorrhizal fungi does penetrate the cortex cells of the plant roots and its hyphae form arbuscules and vesicles inside the plant root. (Synonyms, endomycorrhizal, AM, VAM)

label: coiling_vam
description: Associations that spread predominantly by intracellular hyphal coils within roots.

label: ectomycorrhizal
description: Symbiosis in which the mycorrhizal fungi does not penetrate the cortex cells of the plant roots.

label: ericoid_mycorrhizal
description: A form of arbuscular mycorrhizal relationship only found on plants in the order Ericales. The fungi's hyphae penetrate the plant root but do not form arbuscules.

label: mycorrhizal
description: Plant mycorrhizal association exists, but type not specified.

label: non_mycorrhizal
description: Plants lacking a mycorrhizal symbiont.

label: orchid_mycorrhizal
description: A mycorrhizal relationship specific to orchid taxa, and for most orchids, generally essential for seedlings to establish.

label: subepidermal_mycorrhizal
description: Mycorrhizae where hyphae grow in a cavity under epidermal cells. Only in the genus Thysanotus (family Laxmaniaceae).

label: carnivorous
description: Plant has non-mycorrhizal carnivorous root.

label: cluster_roots
description: Non-proteoid taxa with cluster roots.

label: dauciform_root
description: A type of cluster root found in the family Cyperaceae.

label: fine_roots
description: Particularly fine roots for nutrient uptake.

label: haustorium
description: A highly modified stem or root of a parasitic plant, such as mistletoe, or a specialized branch or tube originating from a hairlike filament (hypha) of a fungus. The haustorium penetrates the tissues of a host and absorbs nutrients and water.

label: hemiparasitic_root
description: Plant with a partially parasitic root.

label: long_root_hairs
description: Plant with specialised long root hairs.

label: parasitic_root
description: Plant with a parasitic root.

label: proteoid_root
description: Also known as cluster roots, are plant roots that form clusters of closely spaced short lateral rootlets and aid in nutrient uptake in nutrient-poor soils; common in members of the family Proteaceae but present in other families as well.

label: root_hairs
description: Plant with specialised root hairs.

label: sand-binding

label: saprophyte
description: Plant that acquires nutrients from decaying biomass.

label: unknown

label: apomixis

label: cleistogamy
description: Autonomous self-pollination within flowers that do not open; does not require a pollinator.

label: geitonogamy

label: allogamy

label: mixed_mating

label: self-compatible

label: self-incompatible

description: Recruitment is restricted to infrequent episodes when favourable conditions occur (for example, unusually wet years), with little or no recruitment in the intervening years.

label: recruitment_intensity_variable
description: Plants sometimes exhibit mass recruitment and other times display gradual recruitment across time.

label: afternoon
description: Flowers open in the afternoon.

label: day
description: Flowers open during the day (diurnal), with no narrower time of day specified.

label: evening
description: Flowers open in the evening.

label: morning
description: Flowers open in the morning.

label: night
description: Flowers open at night (nocturnal).

label: burial
description: Germination increases when seeds are buried in the soil, in darkness.

label: disturbance
description: Germination increases following soil or vegetation disturbance other than fire, such as clearing or soil turnover.

label: fire
description: Germination increases following fire, with the fire-related cue (heat, smoke) not specified.

label: floods
description: Germination increases following flooding or as floodwaters recede.

label: heat
description: Germination increases following exposure to the heat of a fire, typically by cracking a hard seed coat.

label: light
description: Germination increases when seeds are exposed to light, such as at the soil surface or in canopy gaps.

label: rain
description: Germination increases following rain, but the time of year is not specified.

label: rain_autumn
description: Germination increases following autumn rains.

label: rain_spring
description: Germination increases following spring rains.

label: rain_summer
description: Germination increases following summer rains.

label: rain_winter
description: Germination increases following winter rains.

label: smoke
description: Germination increases following exposure to smoke or smoke-derived chemicals from fire.

label: temperature_cool
description: Germination is restricted to, or greatest at, cool temperatures, such as those of a cool, wet winter.

label: temperature_warm
description: Germination is restricted to, or greatest at, warm temperatures.

label: frost_hardy
description: Taxa tolerates severe and/or repeated frosts without significant damage to foliage or shoots.

label: frost_sensitive
description: Taxa tolerates light frosts but is damaged by moderate to severe frosts.

label: frost_tender
description: Taxa is damaged or killed by even light frost.

label: not_applicable
description: Taxa is virtually never confronted with frost in nature and the response is unknown.
